title: Square-zero lifting of homomorphisms from split diagonalizable groups
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $J\subseteq A$ be an ideal with $J^2=0$, put $A_0=A/J$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity section and inverse satisfying the associativity, unit and inverse diagrams; a homomorphism preserves these three operations. For a finitely generated additive abelian group $M$, let $A[M]$ be the free $A$-module on symbols $e_m$, with $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, unit $e_0$, comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$ and antipode $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. Write $D_A(M)=\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$ with the resulting group operations. Let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Every $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$-group homomorphism $u_0:D_{A_0}(M)\to G_{A_0}$ lifts to an $S$-group homomorphism $u:D_A(M)\to G$ whose base change along $A\to A_0$ is $u_0$. Here $G_{A_0}=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ [def-pc-base-change]. No locality, completeness, reducedness or torsion-freeness assumption on $A$ or $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), Corollary B.2.6 and Remark B.2.4, printed pp.285-287: square-zero homomorphism obstruction and its vanishing for diagonalizable groups. This node records their combined infinitesimal existence consequence, not the complete-local lifting theorem. WANTED local archive; online source read.

proof.text: Put $H=D_A(M)$ and $C=A[M]$. Reduction of the basis and of the Hopf formulas identifies $C/JC$ with $A_0[M]$ and $H_0$ with $D_{A_0}(M)$. The kernel $JC$ has square zero: products of its coefficients lie in $J^2=0$. Apply the affine first-order lifting property in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] to $H_0\hookrightarrow H$ and $u_0:H_0\to G$. It gives an $S$-scheme morphism $f:H\to G$ reducing to $u_0$. Moreover $C$ and all its tensor powers over $A$ are free, on tuples of elements of $M$. Tensoring with a free module is a direct sum of the original map, so these algebras are flat. Thus the flatness hypothesis needed for the regular defect is satisfied, without any restriction on torsion in $M$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), proof of Corollary B.2.6, printed p.287, with Proposition B.2.5, printed pp.286-287, and Remark B.2.4, printed p.285. Online source read; WANTED local archive literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-square-zero-hom-regular-defect] to $H,G,u_0,f$. It supplies the $A_0$-module $E=L\otimes_{A_0}J$ with its $H_0$-coaction and the regular defect $c_f\in E\otimes_{A_0}A_0[M]^{\otimes2}$ satisfying $h\cdot c_f(k,l)-c_f(hk,l)+c_f(h,kl)-c_f(h,k)=0$. This is an identity of regular cochains, including over nonreduced bases; it is not a computation only on field-valued points.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), proof of Corollary B.2.6, printed p.287, with Proposition B.2.5, printed pp.286-287, and Remark B.2.4, printed p.285. Online source read; WANTED local archive literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-regular-two-cocycle] over $R=A_0$, with the same $M$, the supplied coaction on $E$, and $c=c_f$. Obtain a regular $1$-cochain $b\in E\otimes_{A_0}A_0[M]$ satisfying $c_f(h,k)=h\cdot b(k)-b(hk)+b(h)$. The correction clause of [lem-sfb-square-zero-hom-regular-defect] constructs $u=f_b=\widetilde b f$ as an $S$-scheme morphism reducing to $u_0$. Its defect is $c_u=c_f-db=0$, so $u\circ m_H=m_G\circ(u\times u)$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), proof of Corollary B.2.6, printed p.287, with Proposition B.2.5, printed pp.286-287, and Remark B.2.4, printed p.285. Online source read; WANTED local archive literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Multiplicativity also gives the identity and inverse diagrams. On the universal identity section, $u(1)=u(1)^2$ in the group $G(A)$, hence $u(1)=1$. On the universal $H$-point over $C$, multiplicativity gives $u(h)u(h^{-1})=u(1)=1=u(h^{-1})u(h)$; uniqueness of inverse gives $u(h^{-1})=u(h)^{-1}$. These are identities of the corresponding morphisms since they were tested on their universal affine points. Thus $u$ is the required $S$-group homomorphism and its reduction is exactly $u_0$.

The item's statement is unchanged and true: it is Corollary B.2.6 combined with Remark B.2.4 for H=D_A(M), which is flat and affine. Step 1: the affine first-order lifting clause of def-sbc-smooth-morphisms gives a scheme map lifting u0, and all A[M]^{⊗n} are free, so the test algebras are flat. Steps 2-3: the defect c_f(h,k)=f(hk)f(k)^{-1}f(h)^{-1}, the cocycle identity and c_{f_b}=c_f-db were verified by hand and agree with B.2.5; the coboundary convention matches Conrad p.284 and Milne 15.1. Step 4: unit and inverse follow from multiplicativity, which is elementary. Defect node: the kernel is Hom(P,JR)=E⊗R0 for flat R. The restriction to flat test algebras is a deliberate and correct choice, since JR is not J⊗R in general, and it suffices because every C^{⊗n} is flat. The kernel clause overlaps lem-sfb-group-space-square-zero-kernel-module; this is not a duplicate, and the node's later split should cite that node for it. Two-cocycle node: degree 2 of Remark B.2.4, true over any ring for any comodule via the M-grading. Tested on M=0 (b=c), E=0 and M=Z/p over F_p.
